terms.definition: A flat, spinning disk of stars, gas and dust with arms winding out from the center — Andromeda is a classic, smooth example with no bar.
The crowded, bright hub at a galaxy's center — Andromeda's is brighter and rounder than the Milky Way's.
terms.function: The old, densely packed heart of the galaxy.

terms.definition: The distance light travels in one year — about 9.5 trillion kilometers. Andromeda is 2.5 million light-years away.
terms.function: The ruler of the galaxy's distance.

terms.definition: A small galaxy that orbits a larger one — M32 and M110 orbit Andromeda like moons.
terms.function: Shows that galaxies can have smaller companions.

terms.definition: Two galaxies falling together and fusing into one larger galaxy — the Milky Way and Andromeda will merge in about four billion years.
